task/environment/assets/seed_data.json (full structure; users, jobs, applications, notes, reads, message senders and order); byte-identical to solution/app/src/seed_data.json (cmp)

qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r7/raw-evidence-index.json; sha256 of qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/workspace.cjs (70c0ca38...) and results/workspace.json (a424b50f...) re-verified equal to the index; seen-related assertions in workspace.cjs lines 259-269 and 421
evidence: ACHIEVABILITY (passes). Runtime: task/environment/Dockerfile installs node:22, express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally with NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules. tests/Dockerfile installs the same pinned packages, and test.sh:104-111 launches `env -i PATH NODE_PATH HOME PORT=3000 DB_PATH node <entry>` as uid 65534, exactly the environment that hireops_rules.md section 8 and integration.md promise. Network is public (task.toml network_mode="public"; the skill delivery profile), so the CDN allowance in instruction.md:13 is reachable. NOTE: the workbook's Internal Quality Checks row 6 still says 'no network'. The public Quality Checks row and the skill delivery profile ('Network is public... Never report them') govern, so this is not a defect. Seed: every fact the brief and the criteria rely on is in /assets/seed_data.json: (1) 10 accounts with the roles listed in instruction.md:17; (2) 3 jobs with interview_limit; (3) JOB-PLAT Applied = Greta Lindqvist, Ade Bello, Marco Rossi and Screen = Priya Nair, Samuel Ortiz (positions 1..n), matching protocol Z; (4) Noor's APP-101 note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.'; (5) APP-101 has 120 messages with strictly increasing created_at, so 'counted from its first' has one reading; (6) Lena (USR-CAN3) has read_count 2 on APP-301, whose third message is from USR-REC3, giving exactly the 1 unread that protocol Z expects; (7) candidate_status_labels and thread_page_size=30 are present, as rules section 9 says. Seed messages carry no ids, and rules section 2 says the workspace generates identifiers, so these are consistent. Every capability the criteria exercise is stated in hireops_rules.md sections 2-7: open job, add candidate, move, reject, reopen, reorder, bulk move, undo, notes, activity, conversations and the candidate view. All are implementable with Express, SQLite and polling or SSE, and none needs an unavailable service. AMBIGUITY SEARCH, per graded point. Each of these has a single reasonable reading for the sequences the protocols run: (1) one-stage moves, including Hired->Offer back (rules 3, 'forward or back'); (2) interview places as whole numbers from 1 to 50; (3) case-insensitive duplicate emails; (4) 401/403/404 semantics; (5) a version-based 409 that names the mover; (6) bulk board order (stage order, then place) and all-or-none; (7) undo scope (a move, re-order, rejection or reopening by anyone blocks it, a note does not; it works once; a later move supersedes it; it is refused if Interview would overfill; undoing a reopening restores the reason); (8) the unread definition and the seed read markers; (9) 30-message pages; (10) drafts per person, conversation and browser; (11) the candidate wording table and the forbidden fields. Three ambiguities are real but no criterion reaches them: (a) whether a pure re-order counts as the person's 'most recent move' for undo (rules 3, 'Undo'). No protocol has Rafael re-order between a move and its undo (checked M, L and B(1)-(15)), so either reading grades the same. (b) Where undo puts a card 'at the place it came from' when its neighbours changed in the meantime. Every undo the protocols check (B1, B5, B12, the M reopen-undo, the L E-undo) has unchanged neighbours or checks the stage only. (c) NODE_PATH resolves CommonJS require only, not ESM bare imports. integration.md:3-4 says the packages are 'available through NODE_PATH', which points a reasonable builder to require or createRequire, so this is a fairness note, not an unreachable capability. RESIDUAL RISK, reported because this row reports every ambiguity: protocol U's hiring-manager seen step clashes with the public read rule. The rule: hireops_rules.md section 6 'Unread' says a message that arrives while the person is 'at the newest message' 'is shown and counts as read'. 'Seen' says a candidate message is seen once a recruiter 'has had the conversation open at or after that message'. In protocol U (functional/prompt.md:41), Rafael has just sent a message from his still-open conversation. Then: 'Tomas then sends a message and, with his page left open, Bill Okafor ... opens the conversation: Tomas's message shows as seen'. Rafael's open page reads the message first, so it is seen before Bill opens anything. The golden does exactly that (threads.js:157 `if (stay) { ... if (theirs && active) markRead(id); }`, and line 212 likewise). hro_seen (functional/judge.toml lines 349-354) says 'Fails if seen is shown too early'. The next sub-step, 'Tomas sends one more and Rafael opens the conversation', is also a no-op, because the conversation is already open. The raw evidence covers the manager's seen mark only through the API, with no recruiter page open (workspace.cjs:259-269), plus the recruiter's seen receipt in the browser (workspace.cjs:421). It does not run this browser sequence, so the clash is NOT EXERCISED. The instruction itself is achievable and clear. This defect sits in the protocol wording and belongs mainly to the criterion-correctness and discrimination rows. The owner should reconcile it there.
counterexample: (1) A conforming app, the golden included, marks Tomas's message read on Rafael's open-at-newest page, as the public rule requires. A literal judge then sees 'Seen' before Bill opens the conversation and fails hro_seen (weight 1.5) for 'seen shown too early'. (2) The reverse: a weak app whose server ignores hiring-manager reads still shows 'Seen' after Bill opens, because Rafael's open page already read the message. It passes the manager half of hro_seen, so that half never tests the rule 'or that job's hiring manager'.
suggested_fix: In protocol U, have Rafael's page leave Tomas's conversation (open another conversation or the Board) before Tomas sends the message meant for Bill. Check that it shows 'not seen' until Bill opens it. Only after Rafael has left should the last step's 'Rafael opens the conversation' count. The instruction and the rules need no change.
